questions.question: Instead of one deployable monolith, a shop runs checkout, billing, and search as independently deployable services communicating over APIs. Which architecture is this?
questions.explanation: Microservices split an application into small, independently deployable services.

questions.question: A team bans mutable state and side effects, building programs by composing map, filter, and reduce over pure functions. Which paradigm are they following?
questions.explanation: Functional programming treats computation as pure function composition without mutable state.

questions.question: Every merge to main triggers an automated build, test run, and deployment to staging with no manual steps. Which practice is this pipeline?
questions.explanation: CI/CD automates integration, testing, and delivery/deployment on every change.

questions.question: A developer packages an app with its exact OS libraries into one image that runs identically on a laptop and a production server. Which container platform does this?
questions.explanation: Docker packages apps plus dependencies into portable container images.

questions.question: Hundreds of containers must self-heal, scale with load, and receive rolling updates across a cluster of machines. Which orchestrator manages them?
questions.explanation: Kubernetes schedules, scales, and self-heals containerized workloads across nodes.

questions.question: A developer renames cryptic variables and extracts duplicated blocks into helper functions; all tests still pass unchanged — behavior preserved, structure improved. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Refactoring improves internal structure without changing observable behavior.

questions.question: A service receives its database connection through its constructor instead of constructing it internally, so tests can pass in a mock. Which design principle is this?
questions.explanation: Dependency injection supplies dependencies from outside, decoupling classes and enabling mocks.

questions.question: A company modifies GPL-licensed code and must release its derivative's source under the same license rather than keeping it proprietary. Which license property forces this?
questions.explanation: Copyleft requires derivative works to keep the same freedoms — the GPL's signature clause.

questions.question: A web app splits responsibilities so one layer handles HTTP input, another owns the data and rules, and a third renders the HTML. Which architectural pattern is this?
questions.explanation: MVC separates Model (data), View (presentation), and Controller (input/flow).

questions.question: A team works in two-week sprints with daily stand-ups, a backlog groomed by a product owner, and a review each cycle. Which agile methodology is this?
questions.explanation: Sprints, stand-ups, and a groomed product backlog are Scrum's defining ceremonies.

questions.question: Two developers edit the same lines of the same file on different branches; on merge, Git flags the overlap for manual resolution. What is this situation called?
questions.explanation: A merge conflict occurs when both branches change the same content and Git cannot auto-merge, requiring a human to choose or combine edits.

questions.question: A function always returns the same output for the same inputs and modifies nothing outside itself. Which functional-programming property does it have?
questions.explanation: Pure functions have no side effects and deterministic outputs, making them predictable, testable, and safe to run in parallel.

questions.question: An API call that charges a card must be safely retried after a timeout without charging twice. Which property makes repeating a request produce no extra effect?
questions.explanation: Idempotent operations yield the same result whether executed once or many times, so retries are safe.

questions.question: Which development methodology requires writing a failing automated test before writing the code that makes it pass?
questions.explanation: TDD follows the red-green-refactor cycle: write a failing test, write minimal code to pass it, then clean up.

questions.question: A library update breaks every caller because callers depended directly on its internal fields. Which design principle of hiding internals behind a stable interface was violated?
questions.explanation: Encapsulation exposes only a stable interface while keeping implementation details private, so internals can change safely.
